comments.text_zh:
> 探索 Go 或 Elixir
我从没见过有人为用 golang 写业务逻辑给出过好理由。如果你写的是真正的服务器，那当然用 golang。如果你写的是某种高速网络互联，用 golang。某个疯狂的缓存系统，当然用 golang。公开的 WS 端点，用 golang。但如果你需要用 golang 访问数据库，而且处理的东西不止是比如一个 session token，那你就选错了，你得回头重新评估。Elixir 正处于“发芽阶段”，我预测未来 5 年会被大规模采用。它确实是一个极优秀的平台，我认识的每一家 fintech 公司至少都伸了一只脚进去试水。我给每个人看这个视频 [1]，他们都说“好吧，靠。” [1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: > explore Go or Elixir I have never seen a good argument for using golang for business logic. If you are writing the actual server then sure, use golang. If you are writing some high-speed network interconnect, use golang. Some crazy caching system, sure use golang. The public WS endpoint, use golang. But if you need to access a DB with golang for anything more than, like, a session token, then you made the wrong choice and you need to go back and re-assess. Elixir is in the "germination phase" and I predict massive adoption in the next 5 years. It is a truly excellent platform, every fintech company I know at least has their toe in the water. Everyone I show this video to [1] just says "well, shit." [1] [VIDEO]

I fell in love with Elixir in 2016 and have been using it full time since, first adopting as CTO in my previous company, now powering my new solo business. It's such a good language, with great community and stewardship, running on a rock solid platform that's so advanced compared to most popular languages today. Erlang was created 38 years ago, and it's good to see the ideas of Armstrong, Virding and Williams to be vindicated today. They simply were too far ahead of their time.

comments.author: lawik
comments.story_title: What I learned from Erlang about resiliency in systems design (2019)
comments.why_zh: 很好地展示 Erlang 韧性与监督树。
comments.quote_zh: 我认为这个能很好地展示 Erlang 的韧性
comments.text_zh: 我觉得这篇文章为了把其中的经验与容器概念和 k8s 对齐，一带而过了最精彩的部分。Erlang 应用/服务不应该崩溃。崩溃发生在监督者树中的某个进程里，而每个监督者都可以有策略，在其子监督者/进程失败时进行恢复。Erlang/BEAM 中的监督并不只是带重启功能的微服务基础设施。它处理应用内部的多种失败，只有所有缓解措施反复失败时，我们才会一路向上崩溃到树的树干，并让整个应用崩溃。如果发生这种情况，Erlang heart 应该把它重新启动，或者调用某种最后的补救措施。或者，如果你在容器里运行 Erlang，这时才会由基础设施层面的东西来重启它。Erlang 中的监督粒度要细得多，并不是重启整个服务。我认为这个能很好地展示 Erlang 的韧性：[VIDEO]
comments.text: I feel like the post brushes past the best parts to line the learnings up with container concepts and k8s. The Erlang application/service should not be crashing. A crash happens in a process in a tree of supervisors and each supervisor can have strategies to recover if its child supervisor/process fails. Supervision in Erlang/BEAM is not just microservice infrastructure with restarts. It handles many types of failures knside the application and only if all mitigations repeatedly fail would we crash all the way up to the trunk of the tree and crash the application. If that happens the Erlang heart should be starting it back up or otherwise invoking some last-ditch mitigation. Or if you run Erlang in a container, that's when you'd have your infrastructural stuff restart it. Supervision in Erlang is much more granular and not about restarting the entire service. I think this gives a good view of Erlang resiliency: [VIDEO]

comments.author: SirGiggles
comments.why_zh: BEAM 及其进程的总体概览。
comments.quote_zh: Sasa Juric 的这个视频比我更能讲清楚 BEAM 的总体概览
comments.text_zh: 不，它们是等价的。我是在当前进程里计算、spawn 了一个进程、通过 Supervisor 启动了一个进程、用 Task.async，还是别的什么，都没有区别。它们之所以等价，是因为它们用的都是 BEAM 进程。Elixir、Erlang 或任何其他使用 BEAM VM 的开发者（至少我自己是这样，因为我不想一概而论）不会在语义上区分 spawn 和 Task.async/3，因为根本不存在这种区别。重要的区分在于调用方是否期待一个返回值；如果不期待，那就可以改用 Task.start_link。我不需要担心函数着色（function colouring），因为这里没有这回事。我也不需要像在 C# 里那样担心 async 与 Task.run 的区别，因为在 Elixir 里没有这种区别。在 Elixir/Erlang 等语言里，要做到异步，就是要做到同步。把它类比到现代后端，我们基本上就是有一个微服务，但每个服务都可以直接调用彼此。我觉得我可能也有点绕着你说了，BEAM VM 之所以与 C# 的 async/await 或 TPL 不同，是因为它对 actor 模型的实现。Sasa Juric 的这个视频比我更能讲清楚 BEAM 的总体概览：[1]。但粗略地 tl;dr 一下：BEAM 进程之于 BEAM，就像操作系统进程之于操作系统。我们不用定义 main 函数，因为 BEAM 中的进程 supervisor 会 spawn 我们定义的进程，而那些就是我们的“入口点”。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: No, they're equivalent. It makes no difference whether I calculate in the current process, spawned a process, started a process via the Supervisor, Task.async, or what not. They are all equivalent in the sense that they use BEAM processes. An Elixir, Erlang, or any other developer using the BEAM VM (or at the very least myself since I don't want to generalize) doesn't make a semantic distinction between spawn and Task.async/3 because there is none. The significant differentiation is whether or not the caller is expecting a returned value, if not then Task.start_link can be used instead. I don't need to worry about function colouring because there is none. I also don't need to worry about async vs Task.run like in C# because in Elixir there is none. To be asynchronous in Elixir/Erlang/etc... is to be synchronous. To equate it to modern backends, we basically have a microservice but every service can directly call each other. I think I also might have been talking around you a bit, the BEAM VM sets itself apart from C#'s async/await or the TPL due to its implementation of the actor model. This video by Sasa Juric can explain better than I can the general overview of the BEAM: [1]. But a rough tl;dr, a BEAM process is to the BEAM, what an OS process is to the OS. We don't define a main function as the process supervisor in BEAM spawns processes we define instead and those are our "entrypoints." [1] [VIDEO]

For example, the schedule is preemptive and keeps processes alive even though there may be rogue processes pegging the CPU.
